name: AlgaPSA
subcategory: PSA for MSPs and IT service firms
tagline: Professional services automation for MSPs: tickets, time, projects, contracts and billing in one system.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A PSA is not one app, it is six: ticketing, time tracking, project tracking, contract and SLA logic, billing, and client portal. An agent can absolutely one-shot the spine of that for one person: clients, tickets, time entries, an hourly or retainer rate, and an invoice PDF at month end. What it cannot one-shot is the billing engine that reconciles prepaid hour blocks, overage tiers, per-asset fees and tax, which is where PSAs earn their money and where quiet arithmetic errors cost you real revenue. It also positions itself as open source, so the honest shortcut for a self-hoster is to deploy it rather than clone it. Build your own if you bill a handful of clients on simple terms; do not if your contracts have tiers.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you log clients, tickets and time entries against a contracted rate, then generate a monthly invoice PDF per client.
requirements: Node 20+ and somewhere to run it, local or a small VPS
A rate or retainer defined per client, since the DIY billing logic is only as smart as what you type
Your own backups of the SQLite file
whatYouLose: Contract logic beyond flat hourly: prepaid blocks, overage tiers, per-asset and per-seat fees, minimum commitments
RMM, documentation and accounting integrations, so ticket and asset data gets typed in by hand
Email-to-ticket ingestion and a client-facing portal with SLA timers
Multi-tech scheduling, dispatch and utilization reporting, which is the whole point once you have staff
Tax handling, invoice numbering discipline, and anything an accountant would call an audit trail
moatNotes: PSAs live or die on the ring of tools around them: RMM agents, documentation, accounting sync. A clone with no integrations is a nicely designed data entry job.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the PSA is the system of record for money owed, and nobody wants their invoicing logic to be a weekend project they wrote themselves. The second a contract has prepaid hours, overage rates or per-device fees, hand-rolled billing turns into a monthly reconciliation chore with real dollars attached. Add staff and you need scheduling, utilization and a client portal, none of which fit in one sitting. Solo consultants with three clients on a flat hourly rate are a genuine exception.
notes: If you only bill hours, the DIY version is fine; if you bill contracts, the clone becomes the bug.
prompt:
Build a local-first PSA-lite for a solo IT consultant. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/psa.db
- Tailwind for styling, plain and dense, no component library
- pdf-lib for invoice PDFs
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth

Data model:
- Client: name, contact email, billing rate (number), billing mode (hourly | monthly retainer), retainer amount, notes
- Ticket: client, title, description, status (open | waiting | closed), priority (low | normal | high), createdAt, closedAt
- TimeEntry: ticket (optional), client (required), date, minutes, description, billable (bool)
- Invoice: client, period start/end, line items snapshotted as JSON, subtotal, status (draft | sent | paid), invoiceNumber (sequential per year)

Screens:
1. Dashboard: open tickets by client, unbilled billable minutes per client this month, total unbilled value
2. Tickets: filterable list, detail page with inline time entry form (date, minutes, description, billable toggle)
3. Time: flat table of all entries, filter by client and date range, editable inline
4. Clients: CRUD, show lifetime billed and current unbilled balance
5. Invoices: pick a client and a month, preview computed lines (hourly = sum of billable minutes at rate, retainer = flat amount plus any hours flagged as overage), save as draft, download PDF, mark sent or paid

Rules:
- Invoiced time entries get locked to that invoice and never appear on a second invoice
- Round time to the nearest minute, show hours to two decimals, do money in integer cents everywhere
- Seed script creates two example clients, five tickets and a dozen time entries

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: email-to-ticket ingestion, client portal, multi-user or roles, RMM or accounting integrations, tax calculation, recurring billing schedules, payment processing.

Deliver a README with setup, the data model, and a blunt list of what this does not do.
